source.title: Detecting Memorization in ReLU Networks
source.authors: Edo Collins; S. Bigdeli; S. Süsstrunk

record.tranche_reason: Applies label randomization to image and audio training sets and reports training accuracy across randomization levels; this is the original intervention relevant to fitting random labels.
record.gate_note: The paper states that training accuracy is 1 for every randomization level. It does not report random-label test error or training time. NMF, PCA, and random-ablation compression results measure sensitivity to activation compression, not the claim versions’ named outcomes; those results are not extracted as claim rows. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: Section 4.1 reports perfect training accuracy under label randomization, including fully random labels for CIFAR-10. This directly tests the fitting component of V1 and the training-fit component of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their NMF-based measure detects memorization and generalization across architectures and datasets, while withholding definite guarantees pending further analysis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses label randomization to induce memorization and reports training accuracy, while the study’s main method analyzes activation compression; it does not report random-label test error.
record.method_sensitivity: The level of label randomization p changes the reported layer-by-layer compression behavior; p = 1 behaves differently from partial or no randomization.

fits_no_version.finding: NMF compression sensitivity distinguishes networks trained at different corruption levels, and the inferred feature-extraction and memorization phases occur across network depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation compressibility and layerwise nonlinearity indicate memorization; depthwise phases do not establish learning order over training.

fits_no_version.finding: On original-label CIFAR-10, NMF compression statistics track the test-loss turning point during training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation compression can provide an early-stopping indicator without demonstrating that real labels are learned before noisy labels.

record.problems: Random-label test error is not reported. Training accuracy is stated in the text without per-level values or an uncertainty estimate; the reported network results average ten initializations per randomization level.
record.rows_left_out: Compression-accuracy curves and their qualitative differences across p are described and shown in Figures 2–4, but measure sensitivity to activation compression rather than the outcomes named by the claim versions. No result rows were omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error under fully random labels is not reported. The optimizer and training hyperparameters are not specified, although the CIFAR-10 networks are explicitly said to differ only in label randomization.
Training time and convergence speed across corruption levels.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Test error rising steadily toward chance with increasing corruption, and evidence that the remaining signal is captured.
Effects of adding or removing explicit regularization on random-label fitting and true-label generalization. The clean-label hyperparameter grid does not establish these comparisons.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels. Layerwise phases and clean-label early stopping do not measure this ordering.

missing.what: The general statement of perfect training accuracy across randomization levels also introduces Fashion-MNIST fully connected networks and SVHN and Urban Sounds CNNs. Record this broader stated coverage separately, with uncertainty about dataset-specific values and corruption endpoints; Figure 4 shows p = 0 through 0.8 rather than p = 1.
missing.locator: Section 4.1, page 5; Section 4.1.2 and Figure 4, pages 6–7; Appendix Table 1
missing.versions: V4 training-fit component; V1 only where fully random labels are established

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Compression accuracy curves are not uncompressed test-error curves across label-noise levels.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label test error at chance is not reported. The study states that label randomization is the only difference between networks, but does not separately report a comparison of training hyperparameters.
Perfect training accuracy across randomization levels is stated, but test error as a function of corruption fraction is not reported. No steadily rising test-error result is stated.

rows.subject: 11-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 with randomized training labels at varying probability p; report training accuracy.

conditions.value: p varies; p = 0 is unmodified and p = 1 is fully random
60 total; ten per randomization level, with different random initializations

rows.value: 1 in all cases, regardless of p
rows.uncertainty: Average results for 60 neural networks; no error bar or interval stated.
rows.note: The paper explicitly attributes the difference among these networks to the level of label randomization. It does not report test error for the fully randomized labels.
rows.check: Add V4: perfect training accuracy across corruption levels bears on its training-fit component. The 60-network average describes the compression analysis; training accuracy of 1 is stated separately for all networks. The text says the CIFAR-10 networks differ only in label randomization, but does not specify their optimizer or training hyperparameters.
